issues.description: The problem statement and UML require Farm.animals to be a List implemented as an ArrayList and initialized in a no-arg constructor, but the provided solution implements Farm.animals as a Set (HashSet). This contradicts the specified collection type and initialization strategy and can confuse students about which collection to use and the expected ordering/behavior of animals (List preserves insertion order; HashSet does not).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the specification: change Farm.animals to type List<Animal>, initialize it as a new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor, and update the getter/setter and methods to use List. Alternatively, if a Set is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to specify a Set and explain the semantic differences (e.g., no guaranteed order) so students are not confused.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML explicitly require the Farm to store animals in a List (specifically an ArrayList) and instruct to initialize an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor. The provided solution, however, declares the collection as a Set and initializes it with a HashSet (types 'Set'/'HashSet' vs expected 'List'/'ArrayList'). This uses different collection type identifiers for the same conceptual entity (the farm's animal collection) and deviates from the explicit requirement, which can confuse students mapping the specification to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement: change the Farm attribute type to List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor; update the getter/setter signatures and any internal usages to use List instead of Set.
